markdown_report:
The best initial experiment remains **stochastic recent-prefix training**: train the corrected GRU4Rec on either its complete observed prefix or a recent suffix, retaining the same immediate next-item target. This is an incremental context-augmentation experiment, with closer precedents than the original report acknowledged.

Starting-point insights: (1) stale-interest recommendations motivate testing dependence on older events; (2) weak connections to recent activity motivate learning from recent evidence; (3) Electronics’ 9.7% wrong-order rate identifies weak sampled separation; (4) mapped embedding similarities near 0.5 do not support a collapse penalty. These observations do not establish that distant context causes errors.

Related-work insights: (1) CL4SRec establishes cropping but uses random-position subsequences and contrastive learning; (2) Tan et al. establish recurrent prefix training and stochastic history modification; (3) Dang et al. directly connect suffix construction, GRU4Rec, losses and supervision density; (4) UFRec/PinnerFormer motivate training interventions, while GRU4Rec objective research provides alternatives. None demonstrates this suffix policy improves the pinned benchmark.

The framework separates three directions: **context exposure** changes histories, **supervision horizon** changes targets, and **ranking objective** changes candidate competition. Supervision density and target weighting cross all three directions and must be controlled.

Three atomic proposals follow. Scores list originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit and limitation.

| Proposal | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-prefix training | 2/6/8/6/4 | Precisely attributable context intervention; feasible extension; directly targets stale interests and weak recent connections; may improve separation; unchanged inference. | Close cropping/suffix precedents limit novelty; persistent preferences may be lost; intent remains unobserved; separation gains are uncertain; matched target exposure needs care. |
| Low-weight two-step auxiliary prediction [UFRec] | 3/6/5/6/5 | Concrete GRU adaptation; reusable representation learning; may strengthen preference connections and sparse discrimination; no auxiliary inference head. | Future supervision is established; benefits may saturate; longer horizons may dilute immediate intent; separation remains unverified; masking and auxiliary weighting add implementation work. |
| Corrected sampled softmax [official GRU4Rec; LogQ paper] | 2/7/4/8/5 | Precise objective adaptation; useful optimization direction; could improve top-list competitors and weak separation; preserves architecture. | Established correction; sampler-specific applicability; only indirect user alignment; harder negatives can be false negatives; exact proposal semantics require care. |

Select recent-prefix training at 0% progress for a bounded comparison. It explicitly targets **revived older interests** and **weak connections to recent activity**, plus Electronics’ wrong-order frequency. These remain hypotheses, not demonstrated benefits.

Choose the training target first. With probability 0.25, sample suffix length uniformly from min(5,n) through n; otherwise retain the full prefix. Preserve order, immediate predecessor, target and negatives. Use matched final-position supervision only if required by the chosen implementation; it is not a GRU4Rec requirement. If the baseline uses dense targets, compare baseline → matched full-prefix/final-target control → cropped/final-target intervention, separating the supervision change from cropping.

Keep full-history inference, seeds, routing, limits, evaluator and selection schedule fixed. Prioritize the matched contrast; later compare deterministic mean-length cropping. Report exposures, shortening frequency, runtime and paired validation differences when available. Bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive selection. Cropping can encourage last-item shortcuts and cannot establish compatibility, redundancy, mood or quantities. No experiment was executed.

idea.description: Stochastic recent-prefix training for the corrected GRU4Rec: occasionally remove older observed events while preserving the immediate next-item target and its negative candidates. Train one jointly optimized GRU model per category; deploy its ordinary scoring head on the complete allowed history without augmentation or score fusion. Treat this as an incremental, controlled context-construction experiment.
idea.motivation: The supplied user diagnosis identifies revived older interests and recommendations weakly connected to recent activity. Occasional suffix training may reduce reliance on distant context when recent evidence is sufficient, explicitly addressing these two user-facing failures. Electronics’ measured 9.7% sampled wrong-order rate and 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin provide model-facing targets. Neither the qualitative feedback nor the quantitative diagnosis establishes that older context causes the failures. The intervention may instead act as regularization or encourage last-item shortcuts; its benefit requires measured validation evidence. Cropping cannot establish equipment compatibility, functional redundancy, quantities, ownership needs or mood.
idea.implementation_notes:
The actual corrected baseline source is absent from the supplied material, so this is an implementation specification rather than a fabricated train.py replacement. Modify its family-specific training-example preparation and loss-position mask; preserve its GRU architecture, scoring head, optimizer, dropout, clipping and predictor writer. Record the resolved configuration, including sampling, target selection, loss reduction and validation schedule. No tools or experiments were executed.

Define an example using a training-history target index j >= 1. Its input comprises only observed events before j, truncated by the baseline maximum sequence length, and its target is history[j]. Choose the user and target before cropping. Retain the baseline user/endpoint distribution when the baseline exposes one target per row. If the baseline uses dense supervision, explicitly document the endpoint rule for BOTH matched final-target conditions rather than claiming that a dense sampler already defines a unique endpoint distribution. A reproducible fallback is to retain baseline user sampling and draw j uniformly from 1 through len(training_history)-1 using the training RNG; skip histories with fewer than two events and record exclusions. Use this fallback identically in both matched conditions. Uniform-user/uniform-endpoint sampling has different target weights from a global mean over dense positions; disclose that difference.

Final-position-only loss is not required by GRU4Rec. Original GRU4Rec predicts successive events throughout sessions; dense causal supervision is compatible with the family, although full-sequence backpropagation differs from original session-parallel updates. If the supplied baseline already uses final-target examples, retain that scheme. If it uses dense targets, explicitly switch BOTH the matched control and intervention to a single final-position target. Compare the supplied baseline separately against that matched control, then compare control against cropping. The latter contrast isolates cropping conditional on final-target supervision. Do not attribute the total baseline-to-intervention difference to augmentation. A future dense implementation could crop individual target contexts, but merely masking early losses in a shared recurrent pass would not remove older context from later states.

Intervention: independently for each row, draw Bernoulli(0.25). When selected, draw integer k uniformly from min(5,n) through n inclusive, where n is the number of observed input events after baseline truncation; retain the last k events. Otherwise keep all n events. Histories of five or fewer events are unchanged. Left-pad the result. Preserve observed-item order and the immediate predecessor. Never insert the target into its input or use subsequent events, held-out interactions or target timestamps. Report the actual fraction shortened because the sampled suffix may equal the full prefix. For n > 5, full-context retention probability is 0.75 + 0.25/(n-4), shortening probability is 0.25*(n-5)/(n-4), and expected retained length is 0.875*n + 0.625. For n <= 5, retention probability is one and expected length is n. Record the empirical retained-length distribution as well.

Use the existing negative sampler and baseline loss on the retained final target. Sample negatives from the unchanged original training context according to baseline rules, before cropping, and preserve those exact candidates for the matched example. Do not recompute exclusions from the shortened suffix. Preserve negative count, distribution, collision handling and replacement semantics; do not introduce hard mining, in-batch candidates, an auxiliary objective or text features in this first trial. Normalize both matched final-target losses over the same eligible rows. If the baseline has a different reduction, retain it in the baseline comparison and disclose the change; global target averaging, per-history averaging and uniform endpoint sampling are distinct weightings.

For a paired experimental design, use separate reproducible RNG streams for baseline sampling and augmentation. Initialize Python, NumPy and PyTorch training RNGs with seed 42 as required. Use a dedicated augmentation generator with seed 42, and draw its Bernoulli and length variables in BOTH matched conditions, applying shortening only in the intervention. This prevents augmentation draws from shifting later target or negative sampling. Preserve the baseline sampling RNG implementation where possible; document any introduced stream separation. Identical seeds alone do not guarantee identical dropout masks or optimization trajectories when shapes or kernels differ. Log target exposures, negative exposures and eligible-loss counts, preferably summarized without storing unnecessary interaction data. Fix the comparison schedule before observing results.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and all four routes: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Preserve supplied splits and the pinned evaluator. Keep maximum epochs 200, exactly 200 batches per epoch, baseline batch size and supplied validation/checkpoint schedule. Respect the host SASREC_EPOCHS setting within that maximum; the host default is 200. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU per trial and account for executed training, GPU profiling, debugging, diagnostics and failed trials within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not inspect other trials, reuse their checkpoints, fetch datasets or weights, or inspect hidden tests. Use only permitted public histories, titles, descriptions and observed timestamps; this intervention needs histories alone. Generic metadata examples do not authorize review text/ratings, item ratings/categories/prices/stores or simulator traits.

Inference uses the complete supplied observed history with baseline maximum-length truncation. Cropping is training-only. Padding must not update recurrent state; zero embeddings alone do not prevent bias-driven updates. Readout must gather the maximum index with a nonzero sequence item, never count-1. Preserve explicit baseline empty-history behavior. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items). Because architecture remains unchanged, the predictor writer should serialize and reconstruct the unchanged architecture and selected checkpoint, retaining all category routing. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Controls are alternative experiments and are never combined at inference. No checkpoint averaging, independent predictors, fitted popularity/transition additions or score fusion is permitted.

Verify that the freshly loaded embedded predictor matches selected in-memory scores in evaluation mode on identical histories and candidates, including empty, short and heavily left-padded cases. Use initial float32 tolerances atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4; investigate discrepancies rather than silently widening them. Inspect ranking agreement alongside score differences, accounting for numerical ties. Keep execution checks bounded and charge GPU use to the shared budget. Fixed-length left-padded tensors can retain approximately the same recurrent compute after cropping, so do not claim a speedup merely because fewer positions contain events. Report elapsed training time and throughput alongside updates, target exposures and scoring work.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), incorporating measured metrics and their definitions. view.model remains the actual trained GRU module. Preserve all host ModelView interfaces, including user_train, meta_data and review_data, without fabricating unavailable fields. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. For matched diagnostics, place the immediate target and negative at the final valid input position and zero-mask other targets in both conditions. Use the SAME unaugmented full-context diagnostic examples, endpoints and negatives for both trained models, matching deployed input conditions. If augmented-context diagnostics are additionally collected, label them separately. Compute margins through log2feats and predict_score and define their final-position population explicitly. Do not compare those aggregates with earlier dense-position diagnostics as if their populations matched. Keep unavailable item-category breakdowns explicitly unavailable. Mapped cosine similarities around 0.5 do not justify a collapse penalty; raw margins also depend on score scale and cannot establish ranking gains.

A bounded initial sequence is the supplied corrected baseline, the matched full-prefix/final-target control if required, and the cropped/final-target intervention. Reuse no checkpoints from other trials. Keep GRU4Rec in every candidate. Avoid the full proposed control grid at 0% progress. If the matched cropping contrast merits further work and budget remains, prioritize a deterministic length control: retain n for n <= 5 and floor(0.875*n + 0.625 + 0.5) most recent items otherwise. This matches the conditional expected length approximately, not the complete length distribution or probability of retaining full context. Report that limitation. Later alternatives include several prespecified fixed recent lengths, uniform versus explicitly defined recency-biased suffix distributions, and length-matched random-position crops. A random-position crop usually removes the immediate predecessor and is therefore a broader context-location control, not a clean test of stochasticity alone. All controls keep targets, negatives, loss, user sampling, updates, batch size and full-history inference fixed. Every new policy is another budgeted selection attempt.

Inspect shortcut risks using bounded, separately labeled sensitivity probes: preserve the final item while shuffling earlier observed items, remove older prefixes, and compare effects by original history length. These perturbations change the prediction problem and reduced sensitivity is not automatically desirable. If budget permits, a separately retrained last-item-context GRU control can test whether gains amount mainly to learning an immediate-predecessor predictor. Cropping can suppress useful persistent preferences, overrepresent short-context learning, exploit popular immediate transitions or create a training/inference context mismatch. Do not infer recovered intent from a favorable sensitivity result.

Select only on the host's equal-weight four-category macro validation HR@10; retain its fixed users, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42 and checkpoint schedule. Log all attempted settings, selected checkpoints and per-category effects. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005, or 0.5 percentage points, and macro HR by 0.00125, or 0.125 percentage points. When host-visible paired per-user hit indicators are available, report the observed macro difference, category differences and a paired category-stratified bootstrap interval. Use an analysis-only RNG with seed 42 and 10,000 replicates; resample the same user indices for both models within each category, compute each category difference and then average the four differences. Take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of replicate macro differences, rather than averaging category interval endpoints. If users overlap across categories, preserve user clusters through coordinated resampling. If only aggregate metrics are available, omit paired intervals rather than inventing outcomes.

These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and fixed candidates. They exclude training-seed variability, candidate-resampling variability and generalization to new categories. They do not correct repeated checkpoint, architecture or policy selection on the same validation set. Record search breadth and treat small selected gains as exploratory; reserve confirmatory claims for the host's untouched held-out evaluation. Do not access test labels or test metrics during search. Sampled HR@10 can order models differently from full-catalog evaluation. Full-catalog recommendations for the twenty training users, five per category, must use the same single category model and existing unseen-item filtering. Interpret simulator feedback qualitatively, tracking rejection reasons only when actually provided. No validation gain, full-catalog improvement, actual intent recovery or online utility improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
# Specification: integrate with the supplied corrected baseline, not a replacement trainer.
# Keep baseline sampling implementation and resolved configuration where possible.
# Both matched conditions consume identical augmentation draws.
augmentation_rng = dedicated_rng(seed=42)

def prepare_training_row(history, target_index, maxlen, apply_crop,
                         baseline_negative_sampler, augmentation_rng):
    # User and endpoint are selected before augmentation.
    # Match their distribution exactly between full-prefix and cropped conditions.
    target = history[target_index]
    original = history[max(0, target_index - maxlen):target_index]
    assert len(original) > 0
    # Preserve baseline negative rules and the original exclusion context.
    sampled_negative = baseline_negative_sampler(
        target=target, original_context=original,
        training_history=history)
    n = len(original)
    selected = augmentation_rng.random() < 0.25
    k = augmentation_rng.randint(min(5, n), n + 1)  # exclusive upper bound
    observed = original[-k:] if apply_crop and selected else original
    sequence = left_pad(observed, maxlen, padding_id=0)
    positive = zeros(maxlen)
    negative = zeros(maxlen)  # Retain actual baseline candidate representation internally.
    last = maximum_index_where(sequence != 0)
    positive[last] = target
    negative[last] = sampled_negative
    record_exposure_and_retained_length(target_index, n, len(observed))
    return sequence, positive, negative

# A scalar-negative adapter is shown above. Preserve any baseline multi-negative
# training representation; diagnosis retains its required B x L negative tensor.
# If the baseline is dense, run its unchanged condition separately.
# Then compare matched final-target conditions; never fuse their predictions.
for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
    seed_training(42)
    augmentation_rng = dedicated_rng(seed=42)
    model = supplied_corrected_GRU4Rec(resolved_baseline_config)
    for epoch in range(min(resolved_host_epochs, 200)):
        for step in range(200):
            # Same users, endpoints and negative sampling in both matched conditions.
            sequence, positive, negative = matched_family_sample_batch(
                apply_crop=trial_crop, augmentation_rng=augmentation_rng)
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            valid_targets = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0)
            loss = baseline_loss(
                features, positive, negative,
                mask=valid_targets, reduction=matched_baseline_reduction)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
        unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint(category)
write_predictor_using_identical_baseline_architecture_and_routing()

# Inference and matched diagnosis: full allowed histories, never random cropping.
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
positions = arange(sequence.shape[1])
last = where(sequence != 0, positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
# Branch explicitly for last == -1 using baseline empty-history behavior.
scores = baseline_empty_handling_or_predict_score(features, last, candidates)
verify_loaded_predictor_matches_selected_in_memory_model()

# Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader),
# metric_definitions, diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) and ModelView.
# Use identical full-context final-target diagnostic examples across models.
# Report this population separately from earlier dense-position diagnostics.

if host_exposes_paired_validation_hits:
    rng = analysis_rng(seed=42)
    differences = cropped_hits - matched_control_hits
    observed_macro_delta = mean(category_mean(differences))
    for replicate in range(10000):
        category_deltas = []
        for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
            indices = rng.choice(200, size=200, replace=True)
            category_deltas.append(mean(differences[category][indices]))
        macro_delta[replicate] = mean(category_deltas)
    interval = percentile(macro_delta, [2.5, 97.5])
    # Replace independent category resampling with coordinated user-cluster
    # resampling if users overlap across categories.
    # This interval does not correct adaptive model/checkpoint selection.

originality.positive: The explicit suffix-length policy, fixed target/negative coupling and full-history deployment define a precise, attributable adaptation tied to the observed complaints.
originality.negative: CL4SRec establishes cropping, Tan et al. establish recurrent history augmentation, and Dang et al. directly study suffix construction with GRU4Rec. The policy is incremental; the earlier score of 3 understated these closer precedents.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could identify when recurrent recommenders benefit from shorter training contexts and motivate better context-selection policies without inference overhead.
future_potential.negative: The intervention may provide ordinary regularization or last-item shortcuts, discard stable preferences, and create context mismatch. Fixed-candidate validation gains would not establish better full-catalog utility.

code_difficulty.positive: The core crop is simple and preserves the GRU architecture, checkpoint format and inference computation.
code_difficulty.negative: The earlier score of 3 understated target-weighting controls, paired negative sampling, RNG separation, supervision-population changes, exposure accounting and predictor/diagnostic verification.

related_work.title: UFRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes auxiliary future supervision and contrastive alignment that disappear at inference.
Motivates separating training interventions from deployed scoring architecture.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not demonstrate recent-prefix augmentation or gains on this GRU4Rec benchmark.
Broader future supervision may emphasize persistence rather than immediate intent.

related_work.title: PinnerFormer
contributions: Uses dense future-action supervision to learn persistent user preferences.
limitations: Its architecture and persistent-preference objective differ from the proposed GRU context intervention.
It does not establish that discarding older context improves immediate next-item ranking.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides family-specific ranking objectives and sampling configurations, including BPR-max and cross-entropy.
Documents batch-derived and additional sampled negatives, whose candidate semantics must be preserved in a controlled context experiment.
limitations: Objective recommendations do not identify the cause of the supplied Electronics failures.
Changing objectives or negative distributions alongside cropping would confound the proposed first experiment.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: The supplied search summary distinguishes the always-included positive from sampled negatives in sampled-softmax correction.
limitations: Implementation requires the actual sampling proposal and inclusion semantics.
It offers an alternative objective experiment rather than evidence for context cropping.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of sampled recommendation evaluation and possible changes in model ordering relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation.
limitations: Does not prescribe a model improvement.
The host evaluator remains fixed; conclusions must remain scoped to its pinned protocol.
Low candidate-sampling variance would not eliminate sampled-metric bias.

related_work.title: CL4SRec
contributions: Uses randomly positioned contiguous subsequence crops with length determined by a fixed history proportion.
Trains augmented views through an auxiliary contrastive objective alongside next-item prediction and retains original capped histories at inference.
limitations: The proposed suffix anchoring, length distribution and absence of contrastive loss differ.
These differences narrow the intervention but do not make sequence cropping novel or establish a GRU4Rec gain.

related_work.title: Tan, Xu and Liu (2016): recurrent recommendation training and augmentation
contributions: The supplied search summary describes training on prefixes paired with immediate next items and stochastic embedding dropout producing shorter effective histories.
Provides recurrent precedents for context augmentation and target-coverage analysis.
limitations: Prefix expansion changes target coverage, while the proposed intervention fixes the selected target and changes preceding context.
Embedding dropout differs from deleting a contiguous older prefix.

related_work.title: Dang et al. (2026): sequence splitting and supervision
contributions: The supplied search summary reports prefix, suffix and sliding-window constructions, including GRU4Rec.
Highlights interactions among splitting, loss and single- versus multiple-target supervision.
limitations: Enumerated suffix construction is a close precedent that limits originality.
Its results do not establish the benefit of the exact stochastic length policy under this pinned Amazon protocol.

related_work.title: Session-based Recommendations with Recurrent Neural Networks
contributions: Establishes GRU4Rec and successive next-event prediction with sampled output candidates.
Clarifies that final-position-only supervision is not a family requirement.
limitations: Original session-parallel recurrent updates differ from full-sequence backpropagation and random-prefix final-target training.
Family membership alone does not make these training procedures equivalent.

related_work.title: Recency sampling for sequential recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary describes target-sampling research with accuracy and efficiency findings for GRU4Rec and other sequential models.
Motivates controlling endpoint probabilities, target exposures and computational cost.
limitations: Changing target sampling is distinct from cropping context around a fixed target.
Reported results do not establish gains for the proposed suffix policy or matched evaluator.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling, relevant to retaining within-user dependence between two models' hit indicators.
limitations: Category stratification and coordinated handling of cross-category users require an explicit application-specific implementation.
A bootstrap over validation users does not capture model-training variation or correct adaptive selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting performance-estimation bias.
Supports recording search breadth and reserving confirmatory claims for untouched evaluation.
limitations: Does not provide a task-specific correction for this adaptive search.
Ordinary post-selection paired bootstrap intervals remain conditional and exploratory.
